text.p: Following are the leading stories in the Pakistani press on Saturday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
DAWN
- China signed a pact with India to slash troops and armaments on their disputed border and assured India that it would not sell nuclear arms or technology to Pakistan.

- China has offered to play a constructive role to help Pakistan and India bridge their differences but maintained that it was for the two Asian neighbours to solve their issues bilaterally through peaceful negotiations.
- Pakistan and European Union are set to start negotiations on a new cooperation pact on December 2 aimed at boosting trade and economic and political contacts.
- Jemima Khan, the wife of former Pakistani cricket star Imran Khan, was fined 200 pounds by a London court for negligent driving.
- Evidence collected by the former Scotland detectives about shooting of Murtaza Bhutto in Karachi on September 20 by the police "points in the direction of a possible conspiracy."

- Financial experts have estimated a revenue loss of more than five billion rupees in 1996/97 (July-June) for all the four federating units, which could go up to staggering 54 billion at the turn of century if Islamabad moves ahead with the concept of "fiscal federalism" for distribution of national resources.
BUSINESS RECORDER
- The federal government has decided to raise minimum deletion target in the engineering sector from 55 to 80 percent within a time frame of 4 years.
- The 1,292 megawatt Hub Power plant, the world's largest private sector power project will be fully operational by January 1, about two months ahead of the schedule.
- Portfolio foreign investment in the local share market fell short of the expected $105 million during January-October since only $54 million poured in.
THE NEWS
- The government is considering new policy for the off-shore deep water oil and gas exploration in Baluchistan and Sindh to attract foreign investment.
- The caretaker government is hiring a reputed international legal firm to investigate the foreign assets of corrupt politicians and bureaucrats, Punjab Governor Tariq Rahim said.
- The Asian Development Bank has approved $200 million credit for phase-II of Pakistan's Social Action Programme.
THE NATION
- Tea manufacturers and importers are contemplating increasing prices of the commodity by 10 to 15 percent by the middle of December.

- Deposed prime minister Benazir Bhutto has said her brother Murtaza Bhutto was murdered as a part of a bigger conspiracy to remove her government, frame her husband in a fictitious case and then blackmail her into quitting politics.
-- Islamabad newsroom 9251-274757
